- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model frequently fails to adjust quickly; anticipate mean reversion and add 1–3% upward bias in next forecast.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility; if 3+ consecutive days show high sentiment volatility, dampen forecast magnitude by 1–2%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 2+ days ≤0.33), model underestimates; add 1–2% upward bias to compensate.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 20–30-day moving average.
